title: Policy process, framing and advocacy craft · Rung 1
subtitle: Who decides, under what authority, and how the question is framed
coverLine: A proposal becomes policy only when an identifiable body acts on it under an identifiable power
subject: S47
author: Dr. Harsh Maheshwari

about.why: Most health proposals fail long before anyone argues about the evidence: they are addressed to no one who can act on them. A tax on sugary drinks, a school-canteen rule and a front-of-pack label each belong to a different body, working under a different law, by a different procedure. This book teaches the reader to find that body and that authority for any proposal, to see the frame a public argument is working inside, and to keep apart two jobs that are easily confused: informing a decision and campaigning for one. It ends with a one-page note on a real Indian proposal that names who decides.
about.howToRead: Read it in order. The early sections build a map of who makes policy in India and how; the later ones use that map on framing and on the difference between research and advocacy. The exercises are decisions, not sums: name the body, name the power it acts under, name the frame. Do them as you go; the note at the end uses all three.
about.prerequisites: Book 0, and above all its Part F: reading a table, checking a reference, telling a premise from a conclusion, and the section on how government works (Parliament and the State Legislatures, the executive, the courts; statute, rule, regulation and notification), which this book builds on directly. No mathematics beyond Book 0 is used, and there are no calculations: the practice sets are exercises in tracing a decision to its body and reading a frame, not arithmetic. Book 4, on food systems, is helpful but not required; where this book uses a programme Book 4 describes, it gives the one fact it needs.

blurb: A short book on how health policy is actually made in India: the bodies that decide, the laws that give them power, the procedures they follow, and the frames that decide which instruments get discussed at all. It closes with the line between informing policy and campaigning for it, and a one-page note on one Indian proposal naming the body that would have to act.
